chapterNote: The first of the fifteen Songs of Ascents, and it starts as far from Jerusalem as a man can get: sojourning in Meshech, camping in the tents of Kedar — the far north and the eastern desert, two places no one could be at once, which is the point: he is among strangers, wherever he is. The trouble is words: lying lips, a deceitful tongue, and he asks what such a tongue deserves and answers himself — a warrior's sharp arrows and coals of the broom tree, the desert's prized charcoal, which by rabbinic tradition on this verse keeps burning within long after the surface has gone dark. The last line is the psalm's whole character: I am peace itself — the Hebrew literally says only 'I am peace' — but when I speak, they are for war. The pilgrimage begins with a man who has had enough of living among liars and wants to go up to the city where the truth is spoken. Every journey to God starts with that homesickness.

1.text: A song of ascents. When I was in distress I cried to the LORD, and He answered me.
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth — ascents]. In my distress [tsarah] I cried [qara] unto the LORD [YHWH], and He heard ['answered', anah] me.
1.notes: shir ha-maaloth (H7892, H4609): the first of the fifteen ascent-songs, most likely sung on the road up to Jerusalem — el-YHWH ba-tsaratah li qarati va-yaaneni (H3068, H6869, H7121, H6030): in my distress I called and He answered. The journey opens with an answered prayer already in hand; the rest of the psalm explains what the distress was.

2.text: O LORD, rescue my soul from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.
2.amp: Deliver [natsal] my soul [nephesh], O LORD [YHWH], from lying [sheqer] lips [saphah], and from a deceitful [remiyah — slack, treacherous] tongue [lashon].
2.notes: YHWH hatsilah naphshi mi-sephat-sheqer (H3068, H5337, H5315, H8193, H8267): rescue my soul from the LIP of falsehood — mi-lashon remiyah (H3956, H7423): from the treacherous tongue. The distress is verbal: the pilgrim is not being beaten but lied about, and it is enough to make him leave.

3.text: What will be given to you, and what more added to you, you deceitful tongue?
3.amp: What shall be given [natan] unto you? or what shall be done ['added', yasaph, the KJV margin] unto you, you false [remiyah] tongue [lashon]?
3.notes: mah-yitten lekha u-mah-yosiph lakh (H5414, H3254): the formula of an oath — 'God do so to you and more also' (cf. 1 Samuel 3:17; Ruth 1:17), whose 'more also' is this same yasaph — turned on the lashon remiyah (H3956, H7423) itself: what will He give you, and what will He ADD, the margin's verb? The tongue is addressed as a defendant.

4.text: Sharp arrows of a warrior, with burning coals of the broom tree!
4.amp: Sharp [shanan] arrows [chets] of the mighty [gibbor — warrior], with coals [gachelet] of juniper [rothem — the broom tree].
4.notes: chitse gibbor shenunim (H2671, H1368, H8150): the answer — a warrior's sharpened arrows — im gachale retamim (H1513, H7574): with coals of the rotem, the desert broom, whose charcoal desert peoples prized for holding its heat — rabbinic tradition on this verse says its embers stay live within after the outside has gone dark. The lying tongue, itself an arrow (cf. Jeremiah 9:8), gets arrows back; the tongue that set fires (cf. James 3:6) gets the hottest fire.

5.text: Woe is me, that I sojourn in Meshech, that I dwell among the tents of Kedar!
5.amp: Woe [oyah] is me, that I sojourn [gur] in Mesech [Meshek], that I dwell [shakan] in the tents [ohel] of Kedar [Qedar]!
5.notes: oyah-li ki-garti Meshek (H190, H1481, H4902): woe — gur, the sojourner's verb — in Meshech, the far north by the Black Sea (cf. Genesis 10:2) — shakhanti im-ohole Qedar (H7931, H168, H6938): among the tents of Kedar, the Arab nomads of the desert to the south-east (cf. Genesis 25:13). No one lived in both; the pair means 'among barbarians, wherever I am' — the exile's word for a home that is not home.

6.text: Too long has my soul had its dwelling with one who hates peace.
6.amp: My soul [nephesh] has long [rav — much, too long] dwelt [shakan] with him that hates [sane] peace [shalom].
6.notes: rabbat shakhenah-lah naphshi im sone shalom (H7227, H7931, H5315, H8130, H7965): MUCH — too long — has my soul tabernacled with a hater of shalom, of peace. The same shakan as verse 5: he has been settled among the unsettled for years.

7.text: I am peace itself; but when I speak, they are for war.
7.amp: I am for peace ['a man of peace', shalom, the KJV margin]: but when I speak [dabar], they are for war [milchamah].
7.notes: ani-shalom (H7965): the Hebrew literally says 'I am peace' — the same idiom as Psalm 109:4, where 'I give myself unto prayer' is literally 'I am prayer'; peace is what he IS — ve-khi adabber hemmah la-milchamah (H1696, H4421): and when I open my mouth, they go to war. The pilgrimage begins here: a man of peace among people who hear his every word as a provocation, packing for the city of peace (cf. Matthew 5:9; Romans 12:18).
